title: Chat Client Pipeline and Middleware
why: In lecture 4 one line, `.UseFunctionInvocation()`, ran the whole tool loop. Today we see that it's a layer around `IChatClient` — the same idea as ASP.NET Core middleware. With layers we add logging, caching and our own logic: counting tokens, guarding the input. And all of it without changing the Controller, only in Program.cs. In a real AI system, cost control, logging and protection live exactly here.
outcomes: You'll explain what a chat client pipeline is: a layer = an `IChatClient` around another `IChatClient`, and how the order of `.Use…()` calls matters
You'll switch on `UseLogging` and see in the log how many requests went to Gemini for one tool question
You'll explain when `UseDistributedCache` helps and when it returns an old, wrong answer
You'll write your own layer with `DelegatingChatClient`: one that looks at the response and one that stops the request

review.q: What is `.UseFunctionInvocation()` and where have we seen a similar idea?
review.a: A layer (middleware) around `IChatClient` — an `IChatClient` that wraps another `IChatClient` · `AddChatClient` returns a `ChatClientBuilder`, every `.Use…()` adds one layer · like ASP.NET Core's `app.UseAuthentication()` for HTTP requests

review.q: `.UseFunctionInvocation().UseLogging()` in Program.cs — which is closer to the Controller? Why does the log show both Gemini requests?
review.a: The first `.Use…()` = the outer layer (close to the Controller) · Logging is inner, closest to Gemini — every request of the FunctionInvocation loop passes through it

review.q: When is `UseDistributedCache` good and when is it dangerous?
review.a: Good — when the answer to the same question doesn't change (FAQ, translation, classification) · dangerous — when the answer depends on changing data (a free table): the cache returns an old answer

review.q: In a `DelegatingChatClient`, what does code see before and after `base.GetResponseAsync(...)`?
review.a: Before base — the request (before Gemini) · after base — the response (tokens, text) · the analogue of ASP.NET Core's `await next()`

review.q: How does a layer stop a request, and why do we put such a layer first?
review.a: It doesn't call `base` and returns a response itself (short-circuit) — nothing reaches Gemini, 0 tokens · first = the earlier we stop, the fewer layers do work

options: A `ChatClientBuilder` — layers are added to it with `.Use…()`
quiz.explain: That's why we can chain `.UseFunctionInvocation()`, `.UseLogging()` and so on directly.

quiz.q: What is a layer (middleware) in Microsoft.Extensions.AI?
options: An `IChatClient` that wraps another `IChatClient` and sees both the request and the response
quiz.explain: The decorator pattern: each layer calls the inner client and returns its result to the outer one.

quiz.q: `.UseA().UseB().UseC()` — which layer is closest to the Controller?
quiz.explain: The first `.Use…()` is the outer layer; the last is closest to the Gemini client.

quiz.q: What does the Controller have to change when we add a layer to the pipeline?
options: Nothing — the change is only in Program.cs
It must take the layer's type instead of `IChatClient`
quiz.explain: The Controller only knows `IChatClient`; how many layers are inside is unknown to it.

quiz.q: You switched on `UseLogging()`, but nothing shows up in the console. The most likely reason?
options: The log level — `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` must be Debug (or Trace) in appsettings.Development.json
The Controller is missing an ILogger
quiz.explain: LoggingChatClient writes at the Debug/Trace level, while the default is Information.

quiz.q: Why is the Trace level dangerous in production?
options: The log gets the full text of users' questions and tool results — personal data
quiz.explain: Trace is for development only — in appsettings.Development.json.

quiz.q: The same question twice on `/ask`, with the cache on. What happens the second time?
options: It calls Gemini again, but for free
The response comes from memory — no request goes to Gemini
An error: you can't ask the same question twice
The cache only works with tools
quiz.explain: The key = messages + options. Exactly the same → the stored response. The log is empty.

quiz.q: Why do we remove the cache from RestaurantApi's `/chat`?
options: A tool answer depends on the database — the cache would return an old “it's free”
quiz.explain: Cache only where the answer to the same question doesn't change.

quiz.q: In a `DelegatingChatClient`, what does code after `base.GetResponseAsync(...)` mean?
options: It runs after Gemini's response — it sees the response
quiz.explain: Before base — the request, after base — the response. Like `await next()` in ASP.NET Core.

quiz.q: TokenCounter sits inside `UseFunctionInvocation`. How many lines does it write for a tool question?
options: As many as there are registered tools
quiz.explain: Every request of the loop passes through a layer that sits inside. Outside — one combined response.

quiz.q: `InputGuardChatClient` stopped a long question. How many tokens were spent?
options: As many as the question has
0 — it didn't call base, nothing reached Gemini
quiz.explain: A short-circuit: the layer created the response itself.

summary: **`AddChatClient` returns a `ChatClientBuilder`.** Every `.Use…()` adds one layer (middleware) to the `IChatClient` — just like `app.Use…()` in ASP.NET Core.

**A layer = an `IChatClient` around another `IChatClient`.** The request goes in, the response comes back. The first `.Use…()` is the outer layer (close to the Controller). The Controller knows nothing about the layers.
**`UseLogging`** — shows how many requests went to Gemini (Debug); Trace writes the full text — development only.
**`UseDistributedCache`** — doesn't call Gemini for exactly the same request. Only for answers that don't change; not in a chat with tools.
**`DelegatingChatClient`** — your own layer: before `base` the request, after `base` the response; without `base` — a stop (short-circuit).
